WHOLE_SCREEN_COHESION.note: The blurred town-derived background connects the page to the illustration, but the sharp rectangular town card and two detached white tiles still read as assets stacked on a menu.

ART_UI_INTEGRATION.note: The town artwork is confined inside a conventional rounded card while the controls below use unrelated opaque panels, borders, and shadows.

TYPOGRAPHY_QUALITY.note: The widely tracked JIBUN CHOICE wordmark feels intentional, but the Japanese subtitle and button labels resemble ordinary web UI typography.

VISUAL_HIERARCHY.note: The large illustrated card and orange play button establish the primary action quickly, although the equally prominent white job-dictionary tile competes for attention.

SPACING_RHYTHM.note: The centered title, illustration, and two-tile row align cleanly, but the tight card-to-tile gap contrasts with the large unused lower half.

DEPTH.note: Background blur, artwork shading, and tile shadows create layers, but the foreground remains a simple stack of flat rounded rectangles.

ICON_CONSISTENCY.note: The book and sprout use delicate brown outline symbols while the play action uses a bold white triangle inside a saturated orange circle.

MOBILE_COMPOSITION.note: The content fits the narrow viewport without crowding, but the two-column utility row produces compressed labels and leaves excessive empty space beneath it.

GAME_PREMIUM_FEEL.note: The town illustration is polished, but the generic rounded cards, restrained type, and sparse hub layout make the surrounding experience feel like an educational web app.

AMATEURISHNESS.note: The oversized empty lower area, mismatched icon weights, generic utility cards, and weak integration between artwork and controls make the screen feel visibly unfinished.

WHOLE_SCREEN_COHESION.note: The game world occupies a narrow centered strip while large plain cream gutters dominate both sides, making the screen look like a mobile page embedded in a desktop canvas.

ART_UI_INTEGRATION.note: The artwork, title, and utility tiles remain separate rectangular modules rather than appearing to emerge from one continuous town environment.

TYPOGRAPHY_QUALITY.note: The English title has controlled tracking, but the small Japanese subtitle and compact tile labels lack enough character and scale for a game hub.

VISUAL_HIERARCHY.note: The illustrated adventure card is the clearest action, but its impact is weakened by the vast surrounding blank canvas and the bright dictionary tile directly below.

SPACING_RHYTHM.note: The upper content is tightly clustered inside the narrow column while most of the viewport below and beside it is unused.

DEPTH.note: The blurred scenic column and card shadows add modest layering, but the abrupt vertical edges against flat cream gutters collapse the illusion of a full-screen world.

ICON_CONSISTENCY.note: The thin book and sprout icons share a muted outline treatment, but they do not visually match the large, solid orange play control.

MOBILE_COMPOSITION.note: The central layout itself retains sensible mobile proportions, but the desktop presentation exposes that it is a fixed-width mobile composition rather than a responsive screen.

GAME_PREMIUM_FEEL.note: The high-quality illustration is undermined by the narrow app column, blank desktop gutters, and familiar web-card styling.

AMATEURISHNESS.note: The fixed-width mobile strip, hard background boundaries, excessive dead space, and disconnected card system make the desktop build look like an unfinished responsive prototype.

top_3_concrete_fixes: Extend the blurred town-derived background across the entire desktop viewport with a full-bleed cover layer, gradient overlays, and no visible hard-edged central strip; keep content within a responsive max-width container above it.

Integrate the hero and navigation by letting the town artwork bleed behind or visually connect into the lower controls, replacing the separate white-card stack with a shared foreground panel or overlapping controls using one border-radius, shadow, and material treatment.

Strengthen hierarchy and rhythm responsively: enlarge the primary adventure card on desktop, increase its separation from secondary actions, reduce the oversized empty lower region, and demote the dictionary and coming-soon tiles through smaller dimensions, lower contrast, and lighter shadows.
requires_human_product_decision: Choose a distinctive branded Japanese display/type system for headings and action labels; the current typography does not carry enough game identity.
Define one icon language for all hub actions, including whether the play control should adopt the same illustrated or line-based treatment as the utility icons.
root_cause: The blurred scenic backdrop improves continuity, but the screen still presents a polished illustration inside a generic card stack, and the desktop layout amplifies that separation by framing the experience as a narrow mobile strip within large empty gutters.
